feedback.observed: Several successive turnover fixes improved empty time, endpoint distance, footprint clearance, and bridge speed, but the user still had to identify that the continuous carrier path communicated the wrong identity story.
feedback.expected: For an identity or continuity complaint, inspect the actor lifecycle and adjacent rendered frames before optimizing another coordinate metric; test what story the uninterrupted trajectory communicates.
feedback.evidence: V21, v25, and v26 passed their numeric turnover checks, yet the v26 source still reused one field-slot actor and moved the UFO directly from the outgoing pickup to the incoming drop. The first diagnosis that traced both facts produced the bounded service-cut correction.
feedback.reproduction: For the next actor-identity motion report, require a source lifecycle trace plus pickup-to-next-action frame sequence before proposing a spatial or timing change.

feedback.observed: The first UFO still slid in from outside, opening sheep 2 through 4 used visible cross-field carrier travel, and the 0.104-second replacement flight still exposed intermediate UFO positions. This made deployment feel like sheep entering from offscreen instead of appearing at their assigned cells.
feedback.expected: Use one point-flash grammar for initial deployment and replacement: no visible intermediate UFO body, no offstage first entry, and sheep revealed only at exact destination cells after the arrival flash.
feedback.evidence: Fresh v29 frames showed the first entry descending from above, opening UFO positions interpolating across the field, and five visible carrier positions during the first turnover. The v30 candidate holds the hidden first UFO at its drop, hides deployments 2 through 6 for the final 0.052 playback seconds before each destination, hides turnover motion for 0.104 seconds, and retains exact-drop sheep transforms.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect adjacent 700px frames around the first arrival, opening deployments 2 through 4, and first, maximum-distance, and final turnovers; reject any offstage slide, visible intermediate UFO or sheep body, missing destination light, or off-drop sheep reveal.

feedback.observed: V30 made deployment and turnover fully hidden point jumps, while first entry, collection approaches, and final exit still communicated different movement rules. The user wanted a brief readable glide at both ends, a very fast green blink in the middle, and exact-drop sheep that never appear to slide from outside the landing point.
feedback.expected: Use one UFO grammar everywhere: short visible departure, fast body-hidden green blink, short visible destination approach, exact stop, operation, repeat. Hold opening sheep at the exact drop until the carrier departs.
feedback.evidence: Fresh public-v30 20ms frames confirmed exact sheep anchors but showed opening sheep beginning to walk during the UFO release hold, which reads as sliding from under the carrier. Source tracing showed deployment and turnover used hidden addJump while collection and exit still called visible addFlight.
feedback.reproduction: Inspect continuous 700px frames for first entry, sheep 3 and 4, the first and later exchanges, early final collection, and upward exit; reject mixed travel grammar, more than 12px visible at either edge, a missing green middle cue, or opening sheep motion before UFO departure.

proposals.change_target: shared UFO entry/service/finale/exit path, actual service timing, body/light visibility split, opening sheep departure hold, deterministic motion checks, and durable README guidance
proposals.cause: V30 hid only selected coordinate changes and applied opacity to the whole moving UFO group, so the green cue disappeared with the body while entry, collection, and exit retained visible slides. Initial sheep also began walking during the carrier release hold.
proposals.candidate_change: Route every UFO entry, service, finale-convergence, and exit leg through one existing-art blink helper: expose no more than 12px at departure, hide only the original UFO body while the existing green light carries the middle, expose no more than 12px into the destination, then stop exactly. Use 0.12 source seconds / 0.156 playback seconds for non-turnover service legs, retain the 0.08 source-second / 0.104 playback-second turnover exchange and fixed finale timing, and delay initial sheep walking until UFO departure.
proposals.discovery_evidence: Fresh v31 adjacent frames show a partial first entrance, green middle blink, exact-drop approach; 2 through 6 deployment repeats; first turnover switches to SHEEP 07 INBOUND before a 0.104-second exchange and exact-drop reveal; collection and upward exit use the same grammar. Sheep 3 and 4 stay fixed through UFO departure. The fixture drops from 48.581 to 44.122 seconds without changing sheep pace.
proposals.reproduction: Run npm run visual:fixture and npm run check; inspect fresh 700px forced-theme adjacent first-entry, deployment 2 through 4, first/later/final turnover, collection, final exit, reduced-motion, 10/28/62 roster, finale, and terminal frames.
proposals.primary_metric: Every entry, deployment, turnover, collection, finale-convergence, and exit leg contains two bounded visible edges around one body-hidden green-light middle, with exact stops and zero opening sheep movement before UFO departure.

proposals.falsification_condition: Reject if any service leg exposes the body across the middle, loses the green directional cue, exceeds 12 visible pixels at an edge, cuts instead of approaching the destination, lets an opening sheep move before carrier departure, reveals a sheep off-drop or in flight, regresses accepted causal/layout/finale behavior, exceeds 50 seconds, or npm run check fails.
